title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2015
desc: A corporation registered in 2015 that never filed has eleven outstanding T2 returns and, usually, a registry problem as well.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2016
desc: Ten years of no returns does not mean the Canada Revenue Agency stopped expecting them. The account stays open and the expectation never lapses.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2017
desc: The usual obstacle to filing nine nil years is not the Agency. It is the belief that the paperwork has to be found first.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2018
desc: A corporation registered in 2018 has been on the corporate rolls for the whole of the period the Canada Revenue Agency publishes figures for.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2019
desc: A corporation set up in 2019 and never used is the most ordinary version of this situation, and the filing obligation started anyway.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2020
desc: A corporation incorporated in 2020 that never traded has six outstanding returns, every one of them reporting nothing.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2021
desc: Many 2021 corporations were registered to hold an asset rather than to trade, and holding is where nil status is most often lost.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2022
desc: A demand to file is a specific letter with a specific consequence, and four outstanding years is about where it tends to turn up.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2023
desc: Mandatory electronic filing reaches tax years that start after 2023, which puts a 2023 corporation on the boundary.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2024
desc: A corporation incorporated in 2024 has never had a tax year that could be filed on paper.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2025
desc: A corporation incorporated in 2025 with a December 31 year-end had its first T2 due on June 30, 2026, so one return is outstanding now.

title: First T2 After Incorporating in 2026
desc: A corporation incorporated in 2026 has no outstanding return. The decisions that matter are the ones taken before the first year-end.
